dashboard.title: Your cupping studio

intro.title: From the cup to a score you can trust
intro.why: A coffee's score shouldn't be a black box. Cata Café makes every evaluation rigorous, traceable, and faithful to the SCA CVA protocol.
intro.what: Run CVA cuppings —descriptive, affective, or combined—, solo or in a group, and get a verifiable, exportable score.
intro.how: Create a session, evaluate cup by cup, and review a transparent score you can audit and compare.
intro.calcLead: Every affective score uses the official SCA CVA formula. No hidden math:
intro.calcSigma: sum of the 8 affective sections (fragrance, aroma, flavor, aftertaste, acidity, sweetness, mouthfeel, and overall), each from 1 to 9.
intro.calcU: non-uniform cups; each subtracts 2 points (with a single cup, uniformity is not evaluated).
intro.calcD: defective cups; each subtracts 4 points (a defective cup is also non-uniform).
intro.calcAnchors: Anchors: all eight sections at 5 give 79.00; all eight at 9 give 100.00.
intro.calcRounding: The result is rounded to the nearest 0.25.
intro.calcGroup: In groups, the community score averages the included evaluations and subtracts the deduction for all cuppers' cups; beyond five cups in total, the deduction is shared out.
intro.calcPerResult: Every result carries its own “How was this calculated?” breakdown with your exact numbers.

stats.title: Session overview
stats.body: A quick overview of the session: how many samples you evaluated, how many cuppers submitted their evaluation, the session average, and the best sample. In group sessions the average uses the community score; in individual sessions, your own scores.

ranking.title: Sample ranking
ranking.body: Samples ordered from highest to lowest score. In group sessions they are ordered by the community score; in individual sessions, by your CVA score. Tap a sample to open its full detail. The ± figure next to the community score is the standard deviation across cuppers: the lower it is, the more consensus there was on that sample.

performance.title: My performance
performance.body: Compares your personal average with the group average. Alignment shows how closely your descriptors match the group consensus: it is informational and does not affect any score.

highlights.title: Featured descriptors
highlights.body: Each sample's sensory profile in one line: the descriptors cuppers agreed on most. Tap to explore all of that sample's descriptors.

tabla.title: Results table
tabla.body: All your ratings by sample: descriptive intensities, affective ratings (1 to 9), and the CVA score. In group sessions, each attribute also shows the community average below your value. Tap a sample's name to see its detail.

grafico.title: Radar chart
grafico.body: The radar chart visually compares your evaluation (solid line) with the community average (dotted line) across the 8 affective attributes. The differences table shows the exact gap per attribute.

porCatador.title: Analysis by cupper
porCatador.body: Visible only to the session owner: the CVA score matrix by cupper, with a three-color consensus semaphore — green within 1 standard deviation of the sample mean, yellow more than 1 SD, red 2+ SD (possible outlier); excluded cuppers are shown in grey. You can exclude a cupper from the group calculation; scores recalculate automatically.

filtros.title: Descriptor filters
filtros.body: These filters govern the whole tab: the cloud, the frequency bars, and the per-cupper analysis. Choose a specific sample or all of them, and a sensory block or the General view, which combines descriptors across the whole sample.

nube.title: Flavor cloud
nube.body: Each descriptor appears once; its size adds up its mentions across every stage (fragrance 1 + aroma 1 = 2). Tap a word to see the per-stage breakdown. The bars below count cuppers per block, so they can differ on purpose. Follows the sample and block filters above.

frecuencia.title: Descriptor frequency
frecuencia.body: How many cuppers chose each descriptor in the selected block. The top 5 are shown; in group sessions only descriptors chosen by at least 2 cuppers are listed. Use View all for the full list.

alineacion.title: Cupper alignment
alineacion.body: Visible only to the owner: what percentage of the group's consensus descriptors each cupper chose. With a sample filtered, it shows alignment within that specific sample.

referencia.title: Reference sample
referencia.body:
The session master can mark one sample as the reference: a shared starting point the others are read against. The tasting starts with it and its quality is pinned at 5 (neither high nor low) on every attribute, so every cupper gives it 79.00 and only describes what they perceive. It sits outside the ranking, the average and the best sample: it is the anchor.
What it adds is context: next to each sample you'll see Δ, the difference between its score and the reference's, always computed on the same kind of score you see beside it (community when visible, otherwise your own).
Reference, group mean and deviation are different things: the reference is the starting point the master chose; the mean is what the group perceived; the deviation (±) is how much the group spread.
referencia.bodyFree:
The session master can mark one sample as the reference: a shared starting point the others are read against. The tasting starts with it and everyone scores it freely, like any other sample. It sits outside the ranking, the average and the best sample.
What it adds is context: next to each sample you'll see Δ, the difference between its score and the reference's, always computed on the same kind of score you see beside it (community when visible, otherwise your own).
Reference, group mean and deviation are different things: the reference is the starting point the master chose; the mean is what the group perceived; the deviation (±) is how much the group spread.

deleteCoffee.title: Delete coffee
deleteCoffee.body: The data that identifies the coffee (name, code, farm, producer, notes and certifications) is erased and it disappears from your list and from sessions. Tasting data — scores, perceived notes, origin, variety and process — is kept anonymously for statistics. Origin sheets of past session samples (farm, producer) and sample labels are not changed. This cannot be undone.

how.title: Perceive, describe, calibrate. In that order.
how.step1Desc: Every person evaluates the cup with the official CVA protocol, at their own pace. Works offline, group sessions included.
how.step1Caption: The method's cupping table, app in hand.
how.step2Desc: The group records intensities and descriptors, cup by cup. The vocabulary is built together.
how.step3Desc: Compare each evaluation with the instructor's reference, measure the deviation and export the PDF report. Convergence, made visible.
how.frame1Aria: Recreation of the affective evaluation screen with a 1-to-9 scale
how.frame2Aria: Recreation of the flavor descriptor selector
how.frame3Aria: Recreation of the score card with PDF report
how.photo2Alt: Cupping table with cups, spoons and flavor wheels; someone logging on their phone.
how.photo4Alt: Live cupping workshop: a group evaluating cups with spoons and notebooks.

features.title: The whole protocol. Zero friction.

item1.title: SCA CVA methodology
item1.desc: The full official protocol across its three sheets: descriptive, affective and extrinsic.

item2.title: Transparent scoring
item2.desc: Every score shows exactly how it was calculated, with the formula in plain view. No black boxes.

item3.title: AI-powered discovery
item3.desc: AI reveals patterns in your cuppings that the naked eye misses: who deviates, on which attribute, and how the group evolves session after session.

item4.title: Built for labs
item4.desc: Works fully offline and syncs the moment the signal comes back.

item5.title: Reports and certificates
item5.desc: A PDF report and certificate per session, ready to hand over.

item6.title: Group calibration
item6.desc: Group sessions against the instructor reference, asynchronously too: each person cups whenever they can.

features.heatmapAria: Deviation map by attribute and cupper, illustrative

audience.title: Built for people who train palates
audience.card1Desc: You run cuppings and workshops and want your attendees to see their progress in data, not just your word for it. Calibrate the group against your reference and hand them their own evolution.
audience.card2Desc: Calibrate whole cohorts, track each student's deviation session after session, and close the course with PDF certificates.
audience.card3Desc: Align your cupping table's judgment before you call a lot.
audience.card4Desc: Keep your panel calibrated, with evidence of consistency.
audience.card5Desc: Group quality control with scores that compare across cuppers.
audience.galleryCaption: Real sessions of the method. Groups from several countries.
audience.photo1Alt: Trainers and method partners gathered around a table, with coffee and notebooks.
audience.photo3Alt: A gathering of trainers in a room overlooking the city.

warmup.title: Sensory Movement

dashboard.title: Sensory Movement
dashboard.body: Kim's five slow movements to help you settle and arrive calmly before smelling and tasting. 3 to 8 minutes, seated or standing.

waiting.title: While you wait
waiting.body: A slow movement helps you settle before cupping. Pick an exercise; if the cupping starts, we take you to the table.

wizard.label: Exercise
wizard.hint: The eyes works best right before smelling. First time: The slow arm. Each cupper does it once before the first sample; it can be skipped.

player.voiceHint: Your device's voice reads every step and cue aloud, so you can keep your eyes closed.
player.stillHelp: No movement and no automatic advance: you attend to your body and move to the next step yourself.
player.soundDemoCaptions: Bell: move · Tick: stop · Bowl: stay still · Double bell: open your eyes
player.soundDemoCaptionsEyesOpen: Bell: move · Tick: stop · Bowl: stay still
player.wakeLockNote: Keep the screen on during the exercise.
player.reducedMotionNote: Reduced motion is on: the figure shows each position without animating it.
player.cueReturn: And now come back, just as slowly.
player.cueOtherSide: And now to the other side.
player.breathOnItsOwn: Let your breathing go on its own.

arrive.posture: Let's begin by breathing. Feet on the floor, hands on your thighs, shoulders loose.
arrive.postureStanding: Let's begin by breathing. Feet on the floor, your arm hanging loose.
arrive.notice: Good. There's nothing to get right, just notice. Let's begin.

breath.inFirst: Breathe in through your nose, with the sound…

closing.still: Good. Stay still, in a neutral position. Notice what the movement leaves behind.
closing.open: And now, whenever you're ready, open your eyes slowly.

warmup.bridge: Now take this attention to the cup. First you feel, then you describe.

reflect.title: Two questions, no hurry
reflect.lead: Take a moment with these two questions. If you like, write what you noticed.
reflect.leadNoSave: Nothing to write: just take a moment with these two questions.
reflect.saved: Saved. Only you can see it.
